notes.loadOrder: course/assets/nav.js injects course/assets/print.css first, then course/assets/nav.css, on every page, before any page stylesheet. print.css owns the palette, the four @font-face sets and the shared primitives (.serial, .plateline, .cut, svg rect rx:0).
notes.themes: Dark is the default on bare :root (color-scheme: dark). Light is :root[data-theme="light"]. There is deliberately no prefers-color-scheme block; the site toggles and persists the choice in localStorage under 'ccarp-theme', applied before paint by nav.js. A third set is defined under @media print.
notes.generation: index.html is generated from tools/hub-template.html by tools/build_hub.py. Edit the template, never the output.
notes.aliases: print.css publishes --paper, --accent, --accent-dim, --good, --bad, --flag, --code-bg as aliases of world tokens because lesson.css, the SVG diagram classes and some hub markup name them. hub-template.html's :root adds --grid, --muted, --text-secondary, --success-text, --critical. nav.css resolves each colour through a course-token / hub-token / literal fallback chain. All are load-bearing.
notes.measures: --prose (28rem) is the reading measure for body-level p/ul/ol; --measure (40rem) is the wider structural width for figures, tables and apparatus. Both are defined in course/assets/lesson.css and nowhere else.

ink-fill.purpose: The solid-ink ground for the one filled block on a sheet. It exists because the bright tint, correct as a hairline, was wrong as a large filled field.

ink-fill-t.purpose: The only text colour permitted on ink-fill.

display.purpose: The credential name in the hub masthead. Bodoni Moda, self-hosted variable woff2. One per page.

headline.purpose: The lesson sheet's h1, set under a 2px plate line.

title.purpose: Section and plate headings, text-wrap: balance.

numeral.purpose: Scores, item counts, minutes, pass mark, days to go. Numbers are display material in this world.

body-read.purpose: Faustina, long-form lesson prose and the practice scenario. Held to --prose (28rem).

body-ui.purpose: Archivo, hub prose, tables, ledger rows, controls.

label.purpose: Question stems and emphasised row text, Archivo 650.

serial.purpose: Chivo Mono. Every label, caption, table head, pill, breadcrumb and field label. Canonical form is the .serial primitive in print.css.

components.name: Calibration Rosette
components.description: The signature component. A guilloche rosette engraved live in canvas from the published domain weights: seven lobes, reach by weighting, green ink by accuracy cut into each lobe's own sector, oxblood cutting the shortfall, a dashed gold ring at the 720 pass mark, bare plate where nothing has been attempted. Source: drawRosette() in tools/hub-template.html. Owns the Results tab only.
components.css: .ds-rosette-plate { margin: 0; border: 1px solid var(--rule-firm); padding: 12px; max-width: 300px; } .ds-rosette-plate canvas { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; } .ds-rosette-plate figcaption { font-family: var(--num); font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: .1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-faint); margin-top: 8px; text-align: center; }

narrative.overview:
A certificate resists forgery by being unreproducibly precise, and so does an honestly weighted score report. This system is built out of the printing craft credentials are actually made from: intaglio line work, guilloche, engraved numerals, security tints, plate serials, counterfoils. Two inks on a tinted stock and nothing more. Structure carries all the ornament — plate lines, ruled indexes, serial strips, a seal — so the instrument feels issued rather than assembled.

Dark is the default and it is the engraved steel plate: a green-black ground with warm ink-white lettering. Light is not white and not cream; it is tinted safety stock. Both themes are first-class and both are shipped in course/assets/print.css; there is deliberately no prefers-color-scheme block, because the site carries its own toggle and persists the choice in localStorage under 'ccarp-theme' (applied before paint by course/assets/nav.js). nav.js also injects print.css on every page before nav.css and before any page's own stylesheet — that injection order is the mechanism that makes one file own the palette and the type site-wide, and it must not be reordered.

Density is high and honest: a workbench, not a brochure. Long-form reading gets a narrow measure and a serif; the workbench gets a grotesque at 13–15px with ruled rows. The world explicitly refuses the arrangement this category ships — equal rounded cards on near-black with one blue accent and a progress bar. There are no rounded corners, no shadows, no gradients, and no progress bar on the learning path: the count is printed instead.
keyCharacteristics: Two inks (intaglio green, oxblood) plus one reserved gold, on a tinted stock
Square corners everywhere, including SVG geometry
Hairline 1px rules with a 2px plate line as the only heavier weight
Four self-hosted faces, each with one named job
Ruled ledger rows instead of card grids
Ornament only in structure — never inside a question body or a timed screen

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Any surface may use exactly two inks — intaglio green and oxblood — over stock and rules. A third hue is not a design decision available here.

rules.name: The Reserved Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold means pass mark or seal, plus the focus ring. If a new element wants gold, it is asking to be a pass mark; if it is not one, it takes ink-faint.

rules.name: The Ink-Fill Rule
rules.body: A filled colour field is printed ink (ink-fill), never the bright tint, and there is at most one filled block per sheet. Everything else is line work on stock.

rules.name: The Bare-Plate Rule
rules.body: An empty state is unengraved plate: the low-density line work with nothing cut into it. Never a grey placeholder fill, never a zeroed bar dressed as data.

rules.name: The Four Jobs Rule
rules.body: Each face has exactly one job: Bodoni engraves display text and numerals, Faustina sets long-form reading, Archivo sets the workbench UI, Chivo Mono sets serials and tabular figures. A face used outside its job is a bug.

rules.name: The Serial Rule
rules.body: Anything that labels rather than speaks — table heads, captions, pills, breadcrumbs, wayfinding, field labels — is Chivo Mono at 11px/0.66rem, tracked 0.14em, uppercase, in ink-faint. Uniform and unmissable.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Figures line up everywhere, not only in tables: print.css applies font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to table, .serial, .fig, time and .num globally.

rules.name: The Two Measures Rule
rules.body: Two widths, defined in lesson.css and nowhere else: --prose (28rem) is the reading measure and constrains body-level p, ul, ol; --measure (40rem) is the wider structural width for figures, tables, callouts, apparatus and pager. Separating them was a deliberate fix — do not collapse them back into one variable, and do not redefine either in another stylesheet.

rules.name: The Ledger Rule
rules.body: Three or more sibling items are ruled rows in one index sharing column tracks. If a design reaches for a grid of equal cards, it has left this world.

rules.name: The Printed Count Rule
rules.body: Progress is a printed count, not a bar. The learning path's track is explicitly hidden; the number stands alone. Short, bounded measures — the plan meter, domain accuracy bars — are 1px-bordered tracks with a flat tint fill and a gold target line, which is a ruled gauge, not a progress bar.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, no text-shadow, no filter: drop-shadow, no gradient, in any state including hover and focus. A surface that needs to read as raised gets sheet and a hairline.

rules.name: The Line-Density Rule
rules.body: Where tone is needed, cut more lines. Value is built from stroke count, not from fills or blurs.

dos: Do let course/assets/print.css own the palette and the type, and keep nav.js injecting it first — before nav.css, before any page stylesheet.

Do ship both themes as real, hand-authored token sets on :root (dark plate, default) and :root[data-theme="light"] (tinted stock), toggled by the site and remembered in localStorage under ccarp-theme.

Do keep every legacy alias (--paper, --accent, --accent-dim, --good, --bad, --flag, --code-bg, and the hub's --grid, --muted, --text-secondary, --success-text, --critical) and nav.css's fallback chains intact.
Do square every corner, including rx: 0; ry: 0 on SVG rects; circles only where the thing is genuinely a circle.
Do separate with a 1px hairline (rule) and structure with a 2px plate line (rule-firm).
Do use ink-fill for any filled field, at most one filled block per sheet, and invert to an empty tint outline on hover.
Do set every label, caption and wayfinding string as a Chivo Mono serial at 11px/0.14em uppercase.
Do hold body-level prose to --prose (28rem) and structural blocks to --measure (40rem), both defined only in lesson.css.
Do keep the built world self-hosted: fonts under course/assets/fonts/ with their OFL licence, no third-party requests.
Do keep pages printing usefully — every stylesheet ships a @media print block that returns the world to black ink on white.
donts: Don't add a shadow, a gradient, or a blur to anything, in any state.
Don't introduce a third ink, and don't spend gold on anything that is not the pass mark, the seal, or the focus ring.
Don't fill a large field with the bright tint; that is what ink-fill exists for.
Don't lay repeated items out as a grid of equal cards, and don't add a progress bar to the learning path — the count is printed.
Don't put ornament — rosette, guilloche, seal, plate border — inside a question body or a timed screen. Those surfaces stay bare.
Don't use a face outside its job, and don't set numerals in anything but Bodoni (display figures) or Chivo Mono (tabular figures).
Don't edit index.html directly; it is generated from tools/hub-template.html by tools/build_hub.py.
Don't remove the OpenDyslexic option or its exclusions for code, figures and SVG.
